gap: None of the results ChatGPT got sets the River 2 Max 500's $0.62 per Wh (EcoFlow US store, $309 ÷ 499 Wh) beside EcoFlow's own RIVER 2 Pro at $0.48 per Wh ($369 ÷ 768 Wh, same day). The Pro costs about 22% less per Wh and gives 54% more capacity for $60 more.
standout_why: I compared against powerbencher.com (cited), powerstations.reviews/power-stations (cited), offgridpick.com and the HSN EcoFlow chart (cited). Powerbencher already has Wh/lb (Jackery 500 v2 40.6, RIVER 2 Pro 42.2) and lifetime throughput (Jackery 512 × 6,000 = 3,072 kWh), but it lists no prices. powerstations.reviews already shows a price-per-Wh column, including the RIVER 2 Max 500 at $309, 0.62 $/Wh, 13.2 lb. Offgridpick has Wh/lb and Wh × cycles but no prices. The HSN PDF is an image and has no readable text. What's left is the same-day price-per-Wh comparison with the RIVER 2 Pro, and the fact that BLUETTI's AC50P is sold out at the maker. Neither is stated on the cited pages I read, but the powerstations.reviews table was cut off at 100,000 characters, so it may list the RIVER 2 Pro.
decides: This confirms the RIVER 2 Max 500 is the cheapest per Wh of the 500 Wh picks I could price at the maker ($0.62/Wh against $0.67/Wh for the AC50P). For a shopper who can carry 18.2 lb, it also shows the RIVER 2 Pro at $369 beats every 500 Wh pick on both cost per Wh and Wh/lb. ChatGPT's 'higher AC output' pick, the BLUETTI AC50P at $339, can't be bought at bluettipower.com today. The Jackery 500 v2 leads on Wh/lb (40.7) and rated lifetime throughput (3,072 kWh to 70%), but I couldn't open a US price, so its cost per lifetime kWh can't be worked out.
